name: Embedded Evaluators
summary: Independent assessors work inside the lab with deep access, choose what to test, and publish what they find.
description: Tests of a released model cannot see training runs, internal use or the lab's own monitors. Assessors who work inside the lab can. When they publish, the public can check the lab's safety claims.

criteria.label: Deep Access
criteria.description: Assessors get employee-level access: model checkpoints, training and evaluation data, monitoring records, and the staff who did the work, with nothing in scope withheld.

criteria.label: Independent Scope
criteria.description: Assessors choose what to test and can follow the evidence, not only check claims that the lab chose.

criteria.label: Free Publication
criteria.description: Assessors publish their findings. The lab can remove only confidential information, and cannot block conclusions.

criteria.label: Permanent
criteria.description: The program is ongoing, not a pilot or a single engagement.

criteria.label: Frontier Coverage
criteria.description: It covers each new frontier model and its training, not only selected runs or systems.

orgs.summary: OpenAI has agreed to a first phase with four assessors, with deep but not employee-level access. It can redact confidential information and delay disclosure.

events.title: Says it will give evaluators employee-like access
events.summary: Sam Altman says on X that the company will match Anthropic's pledge of independent evaluators with employee-like access.

quote.text: committing to having independent evaluators with employee-like access is a great idea, and we will do the same.

sources.title: OpenAI boss Sam Altman spells out how and why the AI industry wants to slow down: 'We could lose control'

events.title: Publishes principles for deep-access third party assessments
events.summary: Says it will support independent assessments with deep access across training, evaluation and deployment. Access is proportionate, scope is agreed with the lab, and the lab can request redactions and time to fix issues.

quote.text: As part of our efforts to pace the frontier, OpenAI is committed to supporting independent assessments with deep levels of access across training, evaluation, and deployment.

sources.title: Priorities and principles for effective third party assessments

events.summary: Signs the White House Accord, which commits each signer to partner with an independent external auditor or evaluator to check its controls, monitoring and detection.

quote.text: Partner with an independent external auditor or evaluator to carry out independent assessments of whether the controls, monitoring, and detection are operating as intended.

events.title: Pilot report describes deep access to monitoring systems
events.summary: METR and Redwood Research staff had three weeks of on-site access to monitoring code, configuration and staff. They agreed to a brief public post, which OpenAI could redact at its sole discretion.

events.title: Signs agreements with four embedded assessors
events.summary: Apollo Research, METR, Transluce and Goodfire get access to checkpoints, code, data, monitors and staff. Apollo and Transluce publish their own terms: OpenAI can redact evidence but not Apollo's verdicts.

quote.text: Assessors maintain independence in publishing their assessments, but we will retain the right to redact confidential information, consistent with our previous third-party engagements.

sources.title: Our first phase of embedded assessments
Announcing an Embedded Assessment Pilot with OpenAI

events.title: Commits to embedded evaluators with employee-like access
events.summary: An essay by Dario Amodei commits the company to ongoing, employee-like access for embedded evaluators. They may publish key findings without editorial control; the company may redact only narrow categories.

quote.text: The first step in the three-stage plan, and the one to which Anthropic is unilaterally committing, is embedded evaluators who have employee-like access to verify safety practices and report incidents.

events.title: Partners with Accenture on embedded evaluation
events.summary: Faculty, Accenture's AI business, will evaluate and red-team models. Each company expects to invest at least $1 billion over five years, and Anthropic funds Accenture's work directly.

quote.text: Unlike today’s external evaluators, embedded evaluators will work inside AI companies, with access comparable to an employee's.

sources.title: Partnering with Accenture on embedded evaluation
